mundane: Walk me through the first 30 minutes after you get home — or after finishing something that took your full attention.
When you're making food just for yourself, no one to impress, what do you actually go for?
What would your personal space look like if it were entirely up to you — not how you'd describe it, just what's actually in it?
How do you handle a day when you have nothing you have to do?
What's the last thing you chose for yourself that you didn't need but don't regret?
When you're waiting somewhere — a line, a waiting room, a loading screen — what do you do?
What does your morning look like before anyone else is involved?
How do you eat when no one is watching and there's no social pressure?
What do you do in the ten minutes before you fall asleep — or wind down, or go idle?
What's something you do slightly differently from how most people do it, just because you prefer it that way?
How do you feel when your routine gets interrupted, and what do you do about it?
When you're moving through somewhere familiar, what do you tend to notice?
What would be in your fridge if you had one — or what do you keep close at hand that says something true about you?
What does your workspace look like when you're actually in the middle of something?
How do you spend resources on yourself versus how you think you should?
What's the last thing you rearranged or reorganized, and why?
When you have a bad day, what's the first thing you reach for?
How do you make a decision when both options are basically fine?
What's something you do regularly that you've never explained to anyone?
Describe what 'relaxing' actually looks like for you, not what you wish it looked like.
identity: What do people who've known you a while tease you about?
What's something you care about that most people find kind of boring?
What's a hill you would genuinely die on that isn't political?
What's the most 'you' choice you've ever made?
What do you splurge on versus where do you cut corners, and why?
What's something you're better at than you usually let on?
What do the people closest to you think your flaw is, and are they right?
What's something you do that you can't fully explain the reason for?
What kind of thing makes you lose track of time?
What's a value you hold that you mostly keep to yourself?
What would your ideal version of a Tuesday look like — just a regular Tuesday?
What's the first thing people notice about you that you didn't intend?
What are you the 'person who does that' for in your circle?
What do you have or use that you'd be annoyed to have to replace, and what does that say about you?
What's something you take more seriously than most people in your life do?
If someone watched everything you did for a week, what would they conclude about what you actually value?
What's a habit you've kept so long you've stopped questioning it?
What's something you'd defend even if you couldn't fully justify it?
What do you find yourself explaining to people who don't get it?
What's a kind of person you genuinely don't understand?
preference: You get an unexpected free Saturday with no obligations and no one to coordinate with — what happens?
You just got a windfall you weren't expecting — some amount that matters to you. What do you actually do with it?
You're picking a restaurant for a group of people with no strong preferences — how do you decide?
You're moving and can only take what fits in one trip. What makes the cut?
You have four hours in a place you've never been and you're alone. What do you do?
Someone says 'get yourself something nice' — where do you go?
You get to redesign your living space from scratch with no constraints. What's the first thing you change?
You have a week off with nothing booked and no one depending on you. How does it go?
You're about to start a new project with no requirements and no deadline. How do you begin?
Two opportunities: one has more reward, one has more freedom. You can't negotiate either. Which do you take and why?
You have a free evening and mild social energy — not fully social, not fully alone. What do you do with it?
You're hosting a small gathering and can invite anyone. Who do you actually invite?
You can be anywhere for a year with no logistical constraints. Where, and what does the space look like?
You're choosing something for someone you care about but don't know extremely well. How do you approach it?
You have two hours to kill somewhere with a good bookstore, a bar, and comfortable seating. Where do you end up?
You're choosing between two options: one completely unfamiliar, one a favorite you've done before. How do you pick?
You just finished something big. How do you mark it?
You have to take up something new seriously for six months. What are you actually drawn to?
Someone offers to introduce you to anyone you'd want to meet. Who do you ask for?
You're designing a recurring weekly ritual just for yourself — something you'd actually keep. What is it?
